text:
maria: quick sync — we need a pattern for actor scoping when requests flow through the inference proxy to Dedicated. Do we propagate the original service actor, issue a minted per-request actor token, or use opaque proxy credentials? Concern: auditing, billing attribution, and least-privilege boundaries.
kevin: my vote: mint a short-lived impersonation token (act_as) that carries the original actor id as a parent claim. keeps downstream services able to do fine-grained RBAC and attribution.
samir: curious about chain length and perf: are we planning one minted token per request? that could be expensive if signing costs/KMS calls are high.
maria: exactly — tradeoff is KMS/signing overhead vs leaking broader credentials. can we cache minted tokens per (actor, target-service, scope) for a short window?
kevin: yes — caching is viable. TTLs should be small (30s–2m) and include request-scoped nonce to avoid reuse for long-lived ops. pseudoconfig: 
```
issuer: auth-signer
claim: {
  sub: "actor:svc:orig-123",
  scope: "invoke:model:read",
  parent: "actor:svc:orig-123",
  exp: now + 60
}
sign_with: signer-key-01
```
samir: alternativ e: carry a proof-of-origin header (signed by proxy using its long-lived key) plus the proxy's token. downstream can validate proof and fetch original actor details from auth service for audit. cheaper but adds roundtrip.
maria: latter reduces signing QPS but means every target must call auth service for full actor map (or we provide a signed blob). preference depends on traffic profile.
kevin: note policy evaluation: if we mint, policies should evaluate against the effective actor (the "sub" in minted token). if we only pass proof header, targets must translate to effective actor before eval. both places need consistent policy semantics.
samir: logging: include request_id, parent_actor_id, and minted_token_id in traces so we can stitch billing and audit events.
auth-bot: ticket created: SEC-5123 "actor-scope handshake for inference proxy" — assigned to @maria and @kevin.
maria: action items: 1) benchmark sign/caching latency (kevin), 2) prototype proof-of-origin header flow vs minted-token flow (samir), 3) draft RFC outlining tradeoffs + sample JWT/claim formats (maria). aiming for RFC by EOW. :calendar:
kevin: ack. I'll add KMS cost estimates and recommended TTLs to the ticket. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — leaving notes here for follow-up.
